item.title: Rover Camera Calibration: The Mathematics of Space Vision
item.description: When we plug a standard webcam into our PC, we assume the image on the screen is a faithful representation of reality. But in space robotics, a camera is not simply an "eye": it is a sensor capturing a 2D array of pixels affected by severe optical imperfections. For a rover on the Moon or Mars to use those pixels to avoid crashing into a crater, we must translate light into pure geometry.
